learning_outcomes.text: At the end of the course, the student will be able to understand the logical organization of a computer, the digital representation of information, the syntax and semantics of the C language, and the fundamental methodologies for structured algorithm design.
The student will be able to apply C language constructs to implement, analyze, and debug software programs aimed at solving scientific and management computing problems.

The student will be able to evaluate and interpret the efficiency and correctness of an algorithm, independently selecting the most appropriate data structures and programming strategies for a specific problem.
The student will be able to communicate design choices clearly and with technical terminology, properly documenting source code and describing software logic.

The student will develop the capacity to independently deepen further aspects of software development, approach new programming languages in the future, and effectively utilize user manuals and technical standards.

syllabus_topics: Foundations of Computer Science and Architectures: information representation, numbering systems and encoding, binary arithmetic, Boolean algebra, basic concepts and models of computer architecture
Algorithms and Programming: introduction to algorithms and programming languages
Introduction to C Programming: structure of a C program, preprocessor directives and macros, variables, constants, primitive data types, and expressions
Control Flow and I/O: formatted input/output, arithmetic and logical-relational operators, control flow structures (conditional and iterative statements)
Modularity: function definition and invocation, parameter passing (by value and by reference), variable scope
Pointers and Linear Data Structures: one-dimensional and multi-dimensional arrays, pointers and pointer arithmetic, relationships between arrays and pointers
Complex Data Structures: strings and string manipulation functions, structures (struct), unions (union), and enumerations (enum)
Algorithms on Arrays: classic algorithmic schemes for searching (linear, binary) and sorting (bubble sort, selection sort, etc.)
Operating System Interaction and Files: the I/O system, file system management (text and binary files), introduction to process management
assessment_rules: The final evaluation is graded on a 30-point scale. Passing the practical test is strictly mandatory to gain access to the subsequent oral examination. The practical test is non-conservative; a passing result shall remain valid exclusively for the current exam session. Failure to register for the oral examination or failure to pass the comprehensive exam will result in the forfeiture of the practical exam grade.
bibliography: Kim N. King, C Programming: A Modern Approach, Apogeo.
Lecture slides, handouts, and exercises provided by the teacher, accessible on the HANDY Unisannio e-learning platform (https://handy.unisannio.it).
